_comment: TWO prompt steps, consumed in order by fake-pi's per-command cursor: epoch one is ISC-299's refused-writes worker, epoch two is a clean read-only turn on the same worker. This exists to pin ONE hazard that a single-epoch fixture cannot see. `state.tool_errors` is CUMULATIVE over a worker's whole life and nothing resets it — deliberately, since harvest reports it as a lifetime total — so a reader that consulted it raw would carry epoch one's three failures into epoch two and condemn a blameless clean turn. Epoch two changes nothing either, so under a cumulative count it satisfies every term of the conjunction and settles `failed`. It must settle `success`. Neither turn writes, so no timing window is needed here.
